article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Evening Brief
article.dek: Lamar is officially out, the board moved with the news, and the Value card went quiet.

items.headline: Lamar is out — the wait is over, Huntley starts
paragraphs: Saturday afternoon, the Ravens downgraded Lamar Jackson from questionable to out for Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET game against the Bengals. The high ankle sprain he suffered October 4 will cost him a third straight game. He was limited all week and took most of the first-team reps Friday, but the ankle wasn't ready.

Tyler Huntley makes his third straight start. He is 1-1 in those starts: an overtime win at Atlanta, then a 13-10 loss at Cleveland. This season he has thrown for 429 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

Here is what changes for you: the morning brief said to wait for the game-time call. That call came a day early. The app's QB row has already flipped to Huntley, and the line moved with the news. No more waiting on this one — if the Ravens-Bengals number works for you, Check it now.
items.takeaway: The weekend's biggest question answered itself Saturday: Huntley starts, so check the number instead of waiting on it.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Saturday downgrades and the Monday report
paragraphs: The Giants head to Houston thinner than they were Friday: tight end Theo Johnson (neck) and safety Jevon Holland (concussion) were both downgraded to out on Saturday. J.J. McCarthy makes his first start for New York shorthanded.

Monday night is nearly set. The Eagles ruled out receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion) and defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen). Running back Saquon Barkley is questionable after returning to full practice Saturday — he has missed two games with a hamstring injury. Tight end Dallas Goedert carries no designation and expects to play.

For Dallas, receiver George Pickens (shoulder) and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) carry no designation after full Saturday practices. The Cowboys ruled out tackle Drew Shelton, receiver KaVontae Turpin and linebacker Dee Winters.
items.takeaway: Monday's picture is nearly set — Barkley is the one name still open, and his call lands with inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Weather: Baltimore stays calm for Sunday
paragraphs: Sunday in Baltimore looks the same as it did this morning: sunny, high around 67, light east wind around 3 mph, rain chance about 10 percent at the 1:00 p.m. ET window.
That is a fact, not a totals edge — nothing in it argues the total either way. The rest of the outdoor slate gets its final check Sunday morning, closer to kickoff.
items.takeaway: Calm and clear in Baltimore on Sunday; the rest of the outdoor slate gets its final check Sunday morning.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Your three cards Saturday evening
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Vikings moneyline -300 (FanDuel), Colts at Vikings. The model's win probability is 78.6% — the most likely to win on the board. The evaluator EV is -0.032, and that's fine: Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate, and that's the job description, not a flaw.
Balanced: Browns moneyline -130 (DraftKings), Browns at Titans. Model 71.9%, EV +0.013. The middle ground: a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor.

Value: no play tonight. The card rotated off Raiders +3.5 this morning and found nothing to replace it with. That is the card doing its job — Value is always the model's +EV play, and when no price clears the bar, it says so instead of forcing one.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate = most likely to win. Balanced = strong without overpaying. Value = the +EV play — and tonight it says pass.

items.headline: Monday night: the model and the market still disagree
paragraphs: Cowboys at Eagles: the model's expected margin has this about a pick'em, while the market board has Dallas -4.5 at both books. Nothing changed through the day — the model didn't budge, and the price barely did.
Tanner McKee makes his second straight start for Philadelphia. When the model says pick'em and the market says -4.5, don't guess — run your number through Check. Monday game? Monday check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: the vig
paragraphs: (Hypothetical example:) Imagine a game where both sides are priced -110. That means every $1.10 you risk wins $1.00, either way. If you bet both sides, you put up $2.20 and get back $2.10 no matter who wins. That missing 10 cents is the book's cut. It has a name: the vig.

What could it mean? A pick has to beat the price, not just pick the winner. A team you like at -110 needs to win more often than the price implies, or the vig eats you over time — even if you pick plenty of winners.
How to apply it: the app's evaluator already prices the cut into every verdict. Type your book's line and price into Check and let the app tell you whether what's left is worth betting.
items.takeaway: The vig is the price of admission — a good pick at a bad price still loses money over time, so Check the price, not just the team.

items.headline: The Lamar move: the board followed the news
paragraphs: This was the day's real move, and it came straight from the injury news. Once Jackson was ruled out, the Bengals spread moved from -1.5 to -3.0 at DraftKings (-2.5 at FanDuel), the total fell from 48.5 to 46.5 at both books, and the Bengals moneyline moved from -115 to -155 at DraftKings while the Ravens went from -105 to +130.

The app caught it: the QB row flipped to Huntley and the market followed in the same refresh. One timing note, and only one: Ravens-Bengals no longer waits for anything. If your book's number works and Check says bet, bet now — waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
items.takeaway: The board caught the Lamar news in the same refresh — the spread, the total and the moneyline all moved together.

items.headline: Elsewhere: a few real moves, the rest ticks
paragraphs: Detroit moved from -3 to -3.5 at both books against Green Bay, and that total rose from 53.5 to 54.5. Seattle moved from -2.5 to -3.0 at FanDuel against Kansas City. The Steelers-Saints total fell from 44.5 to 43.5 at DraftKings, while the 49ers-Falcons total rose from 49.5 to 50.5.
Smaller moves: the Texans spread ticked from -10.5 to -10.0 at DraftKings with the total down from 43.5 to 42.5 at FanDuel, and the Vikings moneyline moved from -290 at DraftKings to -300 at FanDuel.

And the standing reminder: when the board hasn't picked up a move, or your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, tap Check, type in your book's line and price — the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: One news-driven flip, a few real moves, and the rest ticks — and your book's number is the only one that matters.

items.headline: Saturday night's job: check Sunday's prices before the rush
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, and Saturday night is the calm before the Sunday rush. Run each Sunday price through Check tonight — type in your book's line and price and get a bet/no-bet verdict on the number you can actually play.
Start with the 9:30 a.m. ET early game, Steelers at Saints, since its window closes first. Then work through the rest of the slate while the numbers are still Saturday's numbers.
items.takeaway: Check tonight's numbers before Sunday's public money moves them — the early game decides first.
